Aluminum parts, made to your drawing

Custom aluminum housings and structural components. Specify the alloy and finish needed for your application.

Prepare RFQ email
Aluminum intercooler prototypes
Aluminum housings and automotive prototypes

For an enclosure, billet intake component or cooling prototype, review the thin sections and mounting interfaces together with the alloy, temper and finish.

Geometry & process
For lightweight housings, automotive prototypes and multi-feature components, including thin walls and deep pockets.
Size & workholding
Send a 3D model with the overall dimensions and stock size. Enclosure machining considers stress relief, fixture support and the order in which material is removed. Review tool access, clamping space and final interfaces together.
Material & finish
6061/6061-T6 and 7075 appear across billet machining services; 3003 is also offered in the intercooler service. Select the grade and temper for the actual part. Bead blasting, brushing, polishing, anodizing, chemical conversion and powder coating are offered across relevant services. Define color and masking requirements.
Grades to discuss

Aluminum alloys: 6061 · 6061-T6 · 6063 · 6063-T5 · 7075 · 7075-T6 · 2024 · 5083

Specify the alloy and temper on the drawing. Availability and suitability for the part and finish are confirmed in the quotation.

Drawing & acceptance
Drawing requirements

Specify alloy, temper and stock form. For housings, identify wall thicknesses, mounting datums, sealing faces and deep-pocket access.

For anodized or other finished parts, mark masked fits, cosmetic faces and post-finish acceptance dimensions. Treat color requirements separately from geometry.

Inspection and acceptance

Agree checks for flatness, bore relationships and interfaces that control fit. Define surface acceptance using the intended finish.

Specify pressure, leak or assembly tests separately. An automotive prototype in the catalog is not proof of tested vehicle performance.

Agree the measurement method and required records before production.

Quality & inspection
Equipment and order records
Prepare your aluminum machining enquiry

Send a model, drawing, alloy and temper, quantity and finish specification with the intended assembly context.

For fabricated or welded components, identify supplied items and joint requirements. Include any test conditions so feasibility can be checked.

Prepare RFQ email

Add your requirements to the email draft, then attach drawings in your email app before sending.
